props.gloss_en: Rava: and likewise for Shabbat -- [a sukkah of two walls according to their law and a third of a handbreadth] counts as a partition for Shabbat
since it is a wall with regard to sukkah, it is a wall with regard to Shabbat
the wall of a sukkah is like the wall of Shabbat, provided there are not three handbreadths between one reed and the next
and Shabbat exceeds sukkah: Shabbat is permitted only where the standing exceeds the breached, which is not so for sukkah
is it not: the Shabbat of the sukkah exceeds the sukkah -- and we do not say מגו!
no: ordinary Shabbat exceeds the Shabbat of the sukkah
one who roofed over an alleyway that has a side-post -- it is valid
one who roofed over the boards around wells -- it is valid
had he taught us the alleyway, [I would say it is valid] because there are two proper walls; but the boards around wells, where there are not two proper walls -- say no
and had he taught us the boards around wells, [I would say] because there is the name of four walls; but roofing over an alleyway, where there is not the name of four walls -- say no
and had he taught us these two, [they go] from strict to lenient; but from lenient to strict -- say no; [so all three are] needed

schemas.gloss_en: השתא מקילתא לחמירתא אמרינן, מחמירתא לקילתא לא כל שכן -- now that we carry a partition from the lenient domain (sukkah) to the strict (Shabbat), from the strict to the lenient all the more so

objections.gloss_en: איתיביה אביי: ומי אמרינן מגו? והתניא... ויתירה שבת על סוכה... מאי לאו יתירה שבת דסוכה אסוכה, ולא אמרינן מגו! -- the baraita holds Shabbat's partitions stricter than the sukkah's, so a sukkah wall does not thereby count for Shabbat

answered_by.gloss_en: לא: יתירה שבת דעלמא על שבת דסוכה -- the baraita sets ordinary Shabbat against the Shabbat of the sukkah (= p_rava_shabbat_deolam)

objections.gloss_en: אי הכי, ליתני נמי: יתירה סוכה דעלמא אסוכה דשבת, דאילו סוכה דעלמא בעיא טפח שוחק ואילו סוכה דשבת לא בעיא טפח שוחק וסגי בלחי -- דהא את הוא דאמרת: סיכך על גבי מבוי שיש לו לחי כשר! -- on your reading the baraita should also have taught the converse stringency

answered_by.gloss_en: ההוא לא איצטריכא ליה: השתא מקילתא לחמירתא אמרינן, מחמירתא לקילתא לא כל שכן -- that clause was not needed: it follows a fortiori (kv_mechamirta_lekilta)
